name: aivis
description: Check whether AI assistants can find, read and transact with an ecommerce store.
long_description: Three checks against a live store, read-only. (1) robots.txt, distinguishing the crawlers whose blocking removes you from AI answers (OAI-SearchBot, PerplexityBot, Claude-SearchBot, Amzn-SearchBot, Applebot) from training-only crawlers where blocking costs you nothing (GPTBot, ClaudeBot, Google-Extended) — a distinction most published advice gets backwards. (2) A product page's raw HTML rather than the rendered DOM, because most AI crawlers do not run JavaScript: structured data, offer completeness, and how many concrete measurements the page actually gives. (3) The agent-commerce layer (Universal Commerce Protocol over MCP), which decides whether an agent can buy rather than merely describe. Backed by a published survey of 70 consumer brands: 0 of 62 blocked an AI search crawler, and 49 of 70 expose a live agent-commerce endpoint. Every crawler claim is sourced to the vendor's own documentation.

tools.name: check_ai_visibility
tools.description: Check whether AI assistants can find, read and transact with an ecommerce store. Read-only: nothing is created, purchased or uploaded.

tools.name: build_recommendation_test
tools.description: Generate a varied prompt set and scoring rubric for testing whether AI assistants recommend a brand. Does not query any assistant.
